thread:
mike: FYI seeing an 8-12% p95 regression on host-side ingress for short-turn chats after the kernel-selector rollout. Mostly affects seq < 64 requests.
anya: Noted. Which hosts/pools are you seeing it on?
mike: host-group-2 and host-group-5, but canary pool shows the biggest delta.
cheng: Any flamegraphs or pprof outputs?
perf-bot: automated profile snapshot uploaded: gs://perf-artifacts/7443218888/ingress-flame-2026-03-22.html
perf-bot: summary: host-ingress CPU +13% vs baseline, KV cache miss rate +35% on small payloads, syscall writev spikes correlated with smallwrite bursts. Top stacks: parse_stream -> tokenize_chunk -> kv_cache_lookup -> grpc_writev.
sam: Can you paste the top stack snippet?
mike: sure, short excerpt:
```
parse_stream()
  -> tokenize_chunk()
  -> kv_cache_lookup() [hot]
  -> grpc_writev()
```
anya: KV miss spike suggests key normalization or routing change. We rolled kernel-selector v2 last night.
cheng: I ran a quick curl microbench across seq sizes. Median latency went 12ms -> 14ms for seq=32, p95 25ms -> 28ms. Batching heuristics look like they're forming smaller batches because preparse is stalling some requests.
mike: hypothesis: kernel-selector change altered preparse codepath timing which introduces extra memcpys / smallwrites and forces earlier writev syscalls. That increases syscall overhead and breaks batching windows.
anya: quick A/B: can we roll kernel-selector back on one canary node pool and compare? Also try toggling prefix normalization in preparse.
sam: I ran a dev microbench disabling prefix KV normalization; p95 for seq<64 improved by ~9%. Command used:
```
bench/ingress_micro --clients=200 --seq=32 --mode=http2 --iter=2000
```
cheng: instrumented kvcache with normalized-key tags on dev, observed many incoming keys with an extra leading null byte in some client payloads. Looks like a preparse change that didn't strip a control char.
mike: if keys differ by a single leading NUL we would see kvcache miss amplification, explains +35% miss rate.
anya: rolling back kernel-selector on canary now (host-group-2).
perf-bot: deploy: rollback kernel-selector v1 -> v2 (canary) initiated, start time 2026-03-22T14:40:00Z. Observational window set to 15m.
sam: small writev coalesce patch landed in my dev branch; reduces writev syscall count by ~22% in local pprof. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infer/pull/1456 (WIP).
cheng: added kvcache normalized key logging. Sample lines:
[2026-03-22T14:12:01Z] key_in: "\\u0000user:abc" normalized: "user:abc" hit:false
[2026-03-22T14:12:01Z] key_in: "user:xyz" normalized: "user:xyz" hit:true
mike: good catch. If normalization bug is root cause we can hotfix normalization and re-enable selector.
anya: rollback completed on canary at 2026-03-22T14:50:05Z (7443218905). Canary p95 back to baseline after ~10m. Keeping rollback until PR + normalization fix.
mike: action items: 1) keep cluster rolled back (anya) 2) merge kvcache normalization fix + extra tests (cheng) 3) land writev coalesce (sam) 4) add perf dashboard for seq<64 + auto-alert on kvcache miss delta (mike).
sam: I'll open the writev coalesce PR and run a 1h canary stress once merged.
cheng: I'll add unit tests for key normalization and a small end-to-end kvcache integration test.
perf-bot: perf alert suppressed while canary rollback in effect.
mike: I'll draft a short postmortem and rollout plan to avoid flipping selector until we've validated normalization and coalescing. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
